import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Convert embarked and class to categorical variables
data['embarked'] = pd.Categorical(data['embarked'])
data['class'] = pd.Categorical(data['class'])

# Create a bar chart to compare survival rates by sex
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.countplot(x='sex', hue='survived', data=data)
plt.title('Survival Rates by Sex')
plt.xlabel('Sex')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Survived')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_sex.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a box plot to compare fare distribution by survived
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.boxplot(x='survived', y='fare', data=data)
plt.title('Fare Distribution by Survival')
plt.xlabel('Survived')
plt.ylabel('Fare')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_fare.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a bar chart to compare survival rates by class
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.countplot(x='class', hue='survived', data=data)
plt.title('Survival Rates by Class')
plt.xlabel('Class')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.legend(title='Survived')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_class.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a heatmap to show correlation between variables
corr = data[['age', 'sibsp', 'parch', 'fare', 'survived']].corr()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', square=True)
plt.title('Correlation between Variables')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_correlation.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a box plot to compare fare distribution by survived
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.boxplot(x='survived', y='fare', data=data)
plt.title('Fare Distribution by Survival')
plt.xlabel('Survived')

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output_fare.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
